sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店打碟的黑胶唱片时代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每晚都要带着 300 件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，把 DJ 台变成一个充满 50 年历史精美文物的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: As the Israeli-Palestinian conflict enters its darkest chapter in decades, both sides are revoking the same foundational moment in their past, the events of 1948.
sentences.zh: 随着巴以冲突进入几十年来最黑暗的篇章，双方都在重新审视他们过去同一个奠基时刻——1948 年发生的事件。

sentences.en: Today, a look at the meaning and reality of what happened that year.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们来审视一下那一年的意义与现实。

sentences.en: I spoke with David Schipler, the author of a book about the conflict and a Jerusalem bureau chief for The Times at a crucial moment in our understanding of 1948.
sentences.zh: 我采访了戴维·希普勒，他是一位关于该冲突的著作作者，也是《纽约时报》耶路撒冷分社社长，他在我们理解 1948 年的关键时刻发挥了重要作用。

sentences.en: Today, it's Friday, November 3rd.
sentences.zh: 今天是 11 月 3 日，星期五。

sentences.en: David.
sentences.zh: 戴维。

sentences.en: Hi, Michael.
sentences.zh: 你好，迈克尔。

sentences.en: I really want to thank you for making time for us.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你抽出时间接受我们的采访。

sentences.en: My pleasure.
sentences.zh: 我的荣幸。

sentences.en: So, David, in this war between Hamas and Israel, it's feeling extremely important to understand the meaning of 1948, the year when Israel declared itself a nation,
sentences.zh: 那么，戴维，在哈马斯与以色列的这场战争中，理解 1948 年——即以色列宣布建国的那一年——的意义显得尤为重要，

sentences.en: was attacked by its Arab neighbors, and waged a war of independence that displaced Palestinians on a large scale.
sentences.zh: 当时它遭到了阿拉伯邻国的攻击，并进行了一场导致巴勒斯坦人大规模流离失所的独立战争。

sentences.en: Right now, Israel's prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, is describing this current war as a second Israeli war of independence, a second 1948.
sentences.zh: 目前，以色列总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡将当前的战争描述为以色列的第二次独立战争，即第二次 1948 年。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Palestinians in Gaza are invoking 1948 themselves to describe this current conflict because of the potential for another massive dislocation from their homes.
sentences.zh: 加沙的巴勒斯坦人也援引 1948 年来描述当前的冲突，因为他们担心会再次发生大规模的家园流离失所。

sentences.en: That's right, yes.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，是的。

sentences.en: But it feels like for any of these references, these claims and counterclaims, to really make sense, we need to understand why Palestinians,
sentences.zh: 但感觉要让所有这些引用、主张和反驳真正说得通，我们需要理解为什么巴勒斯坦人，

sentences.en: why Israelis are invoking this year and what stories they tell themselves about what 1948 means.
sentences.zh: 为什么以色列人要援引这一年，以及他们对自己讲述了关于 1948 年意味着什么的各种故事。

sentences.en: And then, of course, we need to understand what actually happened that year.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们还需要了解那一年到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: And, David, you arrived in Israel as the bureau chief there in the late 1970s.
sentences.zh: 戴维，你在 20 世纪 70 年代末来到以色列担任分社社长。

sentences.en: And so I'm curious, when you took this job, what were the ways that both Israelis and Palestinians talked about 1948?
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，当你接手这份工作时，以色列人和巴勒斯坦人谈论 1948 年的方式是怎样的？

sentences.en: Well, when I arrived, there were two clashing narratives not overlapping at all.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我刚到的时候，有两种完全不重叠、相互冲突的叙事。

sentences.en: And, you know, when you go to the Middle East, you see immediately how people are imprisoned by history, especially in the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你去中东时，你会立刻看到人们是如何被历史所囚禁的，尤其是在巴以冲突中。

sentences.en: And I kind of think of it as an arsenal of memory, that historical events that happen, and we're in the middle of one right now,
sentences.zh: 我把它看作是一种记忆的军火库，历史事件发生了——我们现在正处于其中之一——

sentences.en: they get really chiseled in stone in terms of the way people think about themselves and about their adversaries.
sentences.zh: 它们在人们思考自己和对手的方式上变得根深蒂固。

sentences.en: And the Israeli-Palestinian conflict is full of these markers of history.
sentences.zh: 巴以冲突充满了这些历史的标记。

sentences.en: 1948 is one of the most important ones, what Israel calls its war of independence, and what the Palestinians call Nakba, the catastrophe.
sentences.zh: 1948 年是最重要的标记之一，以色列称之为独立战争，而巴勒斯坦人称之为“纳克巴”，即大灾难。

sentences.en: I mean, the thumbnail sketch of what happened is that in May of 1948, Israel declared itself a sovereign state,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对所发生之事的简要概述是：1948 年 5 月，以色列宣布成为主权国家，

sentences.en: and immediately was attacked by a crescent of five Arab countries, which erupted into that war of independence, as Israel calls it.
sentences.zh: 并立即遭到五个阿拉伯国家的围攻，从而爆发了以色列所称的独立战争。

sentences.en: And that war created the kinds of upheavals that wars do.
sentences.zh: 那场战争造成了战争通常会带来的那种动荡。

sentences.en: And every year we can see the clash of historical narratives about this particular event vividly,
sentences.zh: 每年我们都能生动地看到关于这一特定事件的历史叙事冲突，

sentences.en: because Israel celebrates a double holiday, and Palestinians mark the event in a different way.
sentences.zh: 因为以色列庆祝一个双重节日，而巴勒斯坦人以不同的方式纪念这一事件。

sentences.en: So Israel has first a day of remembrance or a memorial day, and it is a somber day.
sentences.zh: 以色列首先有一个纪念日或阵亡将士纪念日，这是一个庄严肃穆的日子。

sentences.en: A siren sounds, people pull over to the side of the road, people stop walking in the street,
sentences.zh: 警报声响起，人们把车停在路边，街上行走的人停下脚步，

sentences.en: and they stand for a minute or so in honor of the fallen soldiers and those who died in terrorist attacks.
sentences.zh: 他们静立一分钟左右，以纪念阵亡士兵和在恐怖袭击中丧生的人们。

sentences.en: And then the next day is a day of celebration, the celebration of Israel's independence.
sentences.zh: 第二天就是庆祝日，庆祝以色列独立。

sentences.en: But on May 15th, every year, the Palestinians do what Israelis do on their Memorial Day.
sentences.zh: 但每年的 5 月 15 日，巴勒斯坦人会做以色列人在阵亡将士纪念日所做的事情。

sentences.en: They stand in mourning, silently, to remember that event.
sentences.zh: 他们静默哀悼，以纪念那个事件。

sentences.en: So that is the sort of graphic, dramatic illustration of how the two peoples remember that war of 1948.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是两个民族如何记忆 1948 年那场战争的生动、戏剧性的写照。

sentences.en: Well, describe the two conflicting, contrasting narratives.
sentences.zh: 那么，请描述一下这两种冲突、对比鲜明的叙事。

sentences.en: Well, the key of the Palestinian narrative is the idea that all of the Arabs who left what is now Israel during the 1948 fighting were deliberately expelled by Israeli forces.
sentences.zh: 嗯，巴勒斯坦叙事的核心观点是：在 1948 年战斗期间离开现今以色列的所有阿拉伯人，都是被以色列军队蓄意驱逐的。

sentences.en: The numbers are roughly 700,000.
sentences.zh: 人数大约是 70 万。

sentences.en: And they fled into neighboring countries.
sentences.zh: 他们逃往了邻国。

sentences.en: The Israeli narrative, for many years, and certainly at the time I arrived, was that no Arabs were actually expelled by the Israeli forces.
sentences.zh: 多年来，当然在我刚到的时候，以色列的叙事是：实际上没有阿拉伯人被以色列军队驱逐。

sentences.en: They left of their own accord, either to flee fighting, as people do in wars,
sentences.zh: 他们是自愿离开的，要么是为了躲避战斗，就像人们在战争中所做的那样，

sentences.en: or because Arab leaders advised them to leave pending an Arab victory, after which they could return home.
sentences.zh: 要么是因为阿拉伯领导人建议他们在阿拉伯获胜前离开，之后他们就可以回家了。

sentences.en: So the Israeli narrative is one of moral purity, because they were fighting for their existence as an independent state against Arab armies.
sentences.zh: 所以以色列的叙事是一种道德纯洁的叙事，因为他们是在为作为一个独立国家的生存而对抗阿拉伯军队。

sentences.en: And the Palestinian narrative was also one of moral purity,
sentences.zh: 而巴勒斯坦的叙事也是一种道德纯洁的叙事，

sentences.en: in that they saw themselves as purely victims being expelled deliberately by Israel from land they felt was rightfully theirs.
sentences.zh: 因为他们认为自己纯粹是受害者，被以色列蓄意从他们认为理应属于自己的土地上驱逐出去。

sentences.en: And this is no small dispute, the narrative conflict that you have just described.
sentences.zh: 你刚才描述的这种叙事冲突绝非小事。

sentences.en: No, it goes right into the present.
sentences.zh: 不，它直接延伸到了现在。

sentences.en: In fact, right now, you see many Palestinians who have been urged by Israel to retreat south from northern Gaza to southern Gaza,
sentences.zh: 事实上，就在现在，你看到许多被以色列敦促从加沙北部撤退到加沙南部的巴勒斯坦人，

sentences.en: summoning up this idea of displacement and worrying that they're not going to be allowed to come back.
sentences.zh: 唤起了这种流离失所的想法，并担心他们将不被允许回来。

sentences.en: It's a current issue, and it translates into a yearning to return on the part of Palestinians.
sentences.zh: 这是一个现实问题，它转化为巴勒斯坦人回归的渴望。

sentences.en: Right, a sentiment that we have heard over and over in talking to Palestinians in Gaza over the past few weeks.
sentences.zh: 没错，这是我们在过去几周与加沙巴勒斯坦人交谈时反复听到的情绪。

sentences.en: Yes, and I came across this years ago when I was in the Jabaliyah refugee camp in Gaza, a place which is being pummeled now by Israeli bombing.
sentences.zh: 是的，多年前我在加沙的贾巴利亚难民营时就遇到过这种情况，那个地方现在正遭受以色列的猛烈轰炸。

sentences.en: And I was sitting around with a few guys who were in their 20s, and a kid came in.
sentences.zh: 当时我和几个 20 多岁的小伙子坐在一起，一个孩子走了进来。

sentences.en: He was a lanky boy of 12, and somebody asked him where he was from.
sentences.zh: 他是一个 12 岁的瘦长男孩，有人问他来自哪里。

sentences.en: Now, he had been born in the Jabaliyah refugee camp, but he didn't say that he was from there.
sentences.zh: 他出生在贾巴利亚难民营，但他并没有说他来自那里。

sentences.en: He said, Barbarit, Barbarit.
sentences.zh: 他说：“巴巴里特，巴巴里特。”

sentences.en: I said, I had never heard of Barbarit.
sentences.zh: 我说，我从来没听说过巴巴里特。

sentences.en: Well, a couple of these guys kind of smiled and explained that it had been an Arab village up the coast that had been demolished, really, during the 48 War.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其中几个人笑了笑，解释说那是一个沿海的阿拉伯村庄，在 48 年战争期间被彻底摧毁了。

sentences.en: And his parents and grandparents, as it turned out, as we talked more, had left that village more than 30 years before at that point.
sentences.zh: 随着我们交谈的深入，我发现他的父母和祖父母在那时已经离开那个村庄 30 多年了。

sentences.en: And yet, this kid said that that was where he was from.
sentences.zh: 然而，这个孩子却说那是他的家乡。

sentences.en: That brought home to me how alive the yearning to return was, and how Palestinian children were being taught that they were from Arab towns that had been emptied,
sentences.zh: 这让我深刻体会到回归的渴望是多么鲜活，巴勒斯坦的孩子们是如何被教导说他们来自那些被清空的阿拉伯城镇，

sentences.en: or almost emptied.
sentences.zh: 或者几乎被清空的城镇。

sentences.en: Some had been destroyed.
sentences.zh: 有些被摧毁了。

sentences.en: Some had been converted into Jewish towns.
sentences.zh: 有些被改造成了犹太城镇。

sentences.en: Places that now, given the circumstance, they could not return, because Israel would not let them.
sentences.zh: 鉴于目前的情况，他们无法回到那些地方，因为以色列不会让他们回去。

sentences.en: And yet, that was the dream, to go back to those places someday and live there again, perhaps in the beautiful way that their nostalgia and the family lore described,
sentences.zh: 然而，这就是梦想，有一天回到那些地方再次生活，也许是以他们怀旧和家族传说中描述的那种美好方式，

sentences.en: where the orchards were more fruitful than probably in reality, where life was more peaceful than anything they had experienced and more prosperous.
sentences.zh: 那里的果园比现实中可能更丰饶，那里的生活比他们经历过的任何事情都更和平、更富足。

sentences.en: So that was the dream, and it still is.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是梦想，而且现在依然如此。

sentences.en: It still lives.
sentences.zh: 它依然活着。

sentences.en: So what this boy's answer to your very simple question tells us is not just how ingrained these narratives have become, but how they are passed down generation to generation.
sentences.zh: 所以这个男孩对你那个简单问题的回答告诉我们，不仅是这些叙事已经变得多么根深蒂固，而且它们是如何代代相传的。

sentences.en: Like you said, this boy was not born in that town in Israel.
sentences.zh: 就像你说的，这个男孩不是出生在以色列的那个城镇。

sentences.en: He's probably never even been there.
sentences.zh: 他可能甚至从未去过那里。

sentences.en: But in his mind, that is the only conceivable answer to the question of what is home.
sentences.zh: 但在他心中，那是对“家在哪里”这个问题唯一可想到的答案。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's an idea.
sentences.zh: 这是一种理念。

sentences.en: And the idea is alive and well and very motivating for many Palestinians.
sentences.zh: 这种理念依然鲜活，对许多巴勒斯坦人来说非常有激励作用。

sentences.en: When you arrive in Israel, are you finding comparable versions of an ingrained narrative there around what 1948 and the birth of Israel looks like?
sentences.zh: 当你到达以色列时，你是否发现那里也有关于 1948 年和以色列诞生之类根深蒂固的叙事版本？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对有。

sentences.en: The narrative of the 48 War was a very noble story from the Israeli standpoint.
sentences.zh: 从以色列的角度来看，48 年战争的叙事是一个非常高尚的故事。

sentences.en: Jews were refugees from pogroms and the Holocaust in Europe.
sentences.zh: 犹太人是来自欧洲大屠杀和迫害的难民。

sentences.en: They had come to their biblical land, where there had been a Jewish presence for thousands of years, and they had created a state.
sentences.zh: 他们回到了他们的圣经土地，那里几千年来一直有犹太人存在，他们建立了一个国家。

sentences.en: And their victory was to be celebrated and to be kept in their history and their memory as a time of great accomplishment with all the moral purity that you could imagine.
sentences.zh: 他们的胜利值得庆祝，并被保留在他们的历史和记忆中，作为一段伟大的成就时期，拥有你能想象到的所有道德纯洁性。

sentences.en: So, there was no real questioning in most of the population about the virtue of the 1948 War.
sentences.zh: 所以，大多数民众对 1948 年战争的正义性没有真正的质疑。

sentences.en: And the details of it were all kind of good.
sentences.zh: 而且其中的细节都是好的。

sentences.en: You know, I mean, they treated the Arabs well.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的意思是，他们对待阿拉伯人很好。

sentences.en: They were nice to them.
sentences.zh: 他们对他们很友善。

sentences.en: They didn't force them out.
sentences.zh: 他们没有强迫他们离开。

sentences.en: Some places, they even urged them to stay.
sentences.zh: 在某些地方，他们甚至敦促他们留下来。

sentences.en: In Haifa, there's a story about that, you know, that Arabs in Haifa were urged to stay, not to flee, and all of that.
sentences.zh: 在海法，有一个关于那个的故事，你知道，海法的阿拉伯人被敦促留下来，不要逃跑，诸如此类。

sentences.en: I mean, that's all part of the Israeli narrative.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那都是以色列叙事的一部分。

sentences.en: I remember vividly a convention, a meeting that was in Jerusalem, the first gathering of Holocaust survivors.
sentences.zh: 我清楚地记得在耶路撒冷举行的一次会议，那是大屠杀幸存者的第一次聚会。

sentences.en: They've had more since.
sentences.zh: 后来他们又举行过多次。

sentences.en: And the theme was to pass the torch of memory to their children.
sentences.zh: 主题是将记忆的火炬传递给他们的孩子。

sentences.en: Many of the Holocaust survivors had not talked about their experiences.
sentences.zh: 许多大屠杀幸存者并没有谈论过他们的经历。

sentences.en: The memories were too painful and too ugly to share with their children.
sentences.zh: 记忆太痛苦、太丑陋，无法与他们的孩子分享。

sentences.en: And so, they came, and their children came, and they did talk with them.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们来了，他们的孩子也来了，他们确实和他们谈了。

sentences.en: And they wanted to talk about all their experiences with me, too.
sentences.zh: 他们也想和我谈谈他们所有的经历。

sentences.en: As I walked with a tape recorder through the convention hall, they would flock around me, and they would pull me aside.
sentences.zh: 当我拿着录音机走过会议大厅时，他们会围拢在我身边，把我拉到一边。

sentences.en: And you know what the theme was that many of them wanted to strike in their accounts?
sentences.zh: 你知道他们许多人想在叙述中强调的主题是什么吗？

sentences.en: The theme was resistance.
sentences.zh: 主题是抵抗。

sentences.en: We did not just go willingly like lambs to the slaughter.
sentences.zh: 我们并没有像待宰的羔羊一样心甘情愿地去死。

sentences.en: We resisted.
sentences.zh: 我们反抗了。

sentences.en: And here's how we did it.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们反抗的方式。

sentences.en: We carved out our zones of agency, so to speak.
sentences.zh: 我们可以说是开辟了我们自己的行动空间。

sentences.en: And that conformed with the Israeli idea.
sentences.zh: 这与以色列的理念相吻合。
关于 1948 年的。

sentences.en: Of 1948, to create the state, and to resist, and to be strong.
sentences.zh: 关于 1948 年的，为了建立国家，为了抵抗，为了变得强大。

sentences.en: Jews were no longer going to be massacred.
sentences.zh: 犹太人不再会被屠杀。

sentences.en: They were no longer going to be slaughtered.
sentences.zh: 他们不再会被杀害。

sentences.en: They were no longer going to be gassed and imprisoned.
sentences.zh: 他们不再会被毒气毒死和监禁。

sentences.en: They were going to fight back.
sentences.zh: 他们要反击。

sentences.en: They had the weapons.
sentences.zh: 他们有武器。

sentences.en: They had the will.
sentences.zh: 他们有意志。

sentences.en: They had the strength.
sentences.zh: 他们有力量。

sentences.en: We are here.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里。

sentences.en: This is where we will stay.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们将要留下的地方。

sentences.en: We are not going anywhere.
sentences.zh: 我们哪儿也不去。

sentences.en: So this, to me, represents the core of the Israeli-Jewish attachment to that history.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，这代表了以色列犹太人对那段历史的核心依恋。

sentences.en: Okay, so these are the two very ingrained, seemingly immovable narratives that you're absorbing in your time in Israel.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以这些就是你在以色列期间吸收的两种根深蒂固、看似不可动摇的叙事。

sentences.en: Yes, that's right.

sentences.en: And when I first got there in 1979, I came with a sensitivity to how people can manipulate history.

sentences.en: So there was a Zionist movement, a push for a Jewish state, long before World War II and the HolocauSt.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Yes, that's right.
sentences.zh: 你知道，第二次世界大战于1945年结束。

sentences.en: You know, World War II ended in 1945.
sentences.zh: 六百万犹太人被纳粹屠杀。

sentences.en: Six million Jews had been slaughtered by the Nazis.
sentences.zh: 还有许多许多人担心自己的生命安全，沦为难民。

sentences.en: Many, many others had feared for their lives and become refugees.
sentences.zh: 在国际上，人们对犹太人深表同情，并支持他们应该拥有一个避难所、一个家园的想法，

sentences.en: And internationally, there was a great sympathy for the Jews and for the idea that they ought to have a refuge, a homeland,
sentences.zh: 根据犹太复国主义者的说法，一个自然的家园就在圣经记载的土地上。

sentences.en: a natural homeland, according to the Zionists, was in the biblical lands.
sentences.zh: 因此，1947年，联合国通过了一项分治计划，将地中海和约旦河之间的土地划分为两个国家，一个阿拉伯国家和一个犹太国家。

sentences.en: So in 1947, the United Nations passed a partition plan, dividing that land between the Mediterranean and the Jordan River into two states, an Arab state and a Jewish state.
sentences.zh: 拿走这片英国控制的土地，基本上分给在那里的犹太人一部分，分给在那里的阿拉伯人口一部分。

sentences.en: Take this British-controlled land and basically give some to these Jews who were there and some to the Arab population that was there.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是这样。

sentences.en: That's right, exactly.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看1947年那项分治计划的边界，它看起来就像一个被操纵的国会选区。

sentences.en: And if you look at the boundaries of that partition plan in 1947, it looks like a gerrymandered congressional district.
sentences.zh: 但他们基本上遵循了该地区犹太人口的分布界线。

sentences.en: But they basically followed the lines of the Jewish population in the area.
sentences.zh: 他们将主要是阿拉伯人的地区排除在犹太国家之外。

sentences.en: They left out of the Jewish state areas that were mostly Arab.
sentences.zh: 但双方都有混合居住的情况。

sentences.en: But there was mixture on both sides.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在被指定为犹太国家的地区肯定有阿拉伯人。

sentences.en: I mean, there were certainly Arabs in the parts that were designated as a Jewish state.
sentences.zh: 后来发生的事情是，犹太武装力量

sentences.en: What happened then was that the Jewish forces
sentences.zh: 接受了分治计划，而阿拉伯人没有。

sentences.en: accepted the partition plan and the Arabs did not.
sentences.zh: 该地区的阿拉伯人拒绝了它，阿拉伯国家也拒绝了它。

sentences.en: The Arabs within the area rejected it and Arab countries rejected it.
sentences.zh: 据我所读的历史，犹太人接受了这次分治，因为他们觉得自己在军事上相当弱，认为这是他们能得到的最好结果，

sentences.en: The Jews accepted this partition from what I've read in history because they felt fairly weak militarily and figured this was as good as they could get
sentences.zh: 而且他们将获得一个国家。

sentences.en: and they were going to get a state.
sentences.zh: 我认为阿拉伯国家当时有一种感觉，认为他们在军事上更胜一筹，可以轻易击败这支乌合之众的军队，

sentences.en: And I think there was a sense that the Arab countries thought that they were superior militarily and could easily defeat this ragtag army
sentences.zh: 这支军队的武器大多来自捷克斯洛伐克。

sentences.en: that was getting its weapons from Czechoslovakia, mostly.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，他们当时没有从美国得到任何武器。

sentences.en: They did not get any weapons from the United States, by the way, at that time.
sentences.zh: 美国当时试图置身事外。

sentences.en: The U.S.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它只有一点点空军的骨架，但你知道，它不会成为什么强大的敌人，你知道，一个真正的对手。

sentences.en: was trying to stay out of it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们可能会被碾压。

sentences.en: You know, it had a little kind of skeleton of an air force, but, you know, it wasn't going to be much of a foe, you know, a real opponent.
sentences.zh: 我想这可能是当时的假设。

sentences.en: I mean, they could get rolled over.
sentences.zh: 而且，从内部来看，当地的阿拉伯人也不想要这个犹太国家，因为他们是闯入者。

sentences.en: And I think that was probably the assumption at the time.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And also there was just from inside, too, the local Arabs didn't want this Jewish state either because they were interlopers.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They were Europeans coming in, foreigners, not indigenous to the land, and therefore had no real right there.
sentences.zh: 当时进入那里的欧洲人是外来者，并非这片土地的原住民，因此他们在那儿并没有真正的权利。

sentences.en: They were not accepting of that.
sentences.zh: 他们对此并不接受。

sentences.en: And in May of 1948, the time at which the mandate by the British was to end, the British withdrew, and Israel declared its independence and then was attacked.
sentences.zh: 1948年5月，即英国托管期即将结束之时，英军撤离，以色列宣布独立，随后便遭到了攻击。

sentences.en: Instantly.
sentences.zh: 立刻就遭到了攻击。

sentences.en: Yes, that's correct.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Arab armies from Lebanon, Syria, Jordan, Egypt, and Saudi Arabia, too, which sent a unit under Egyptian control, attacked.
sentences.zh: 来自黎巴嫩、叙利亚、约旦、埃及以及沙特阿拉伯的阿拉伯军队——沙特还派了一支受埃及指挥的部队——发起了进攻。

sentences.en: And the 1948 war began.
sentences.zh: 1948年战争由此爆发。

sentences.en: And what happens once the Arab neighbors of this new nation of Israel attack?
sentences.zh: 那么，当这个新生的以色列国家的阿拉伯邻国发起攻击后，情况如何呢？

sentences.en: There was a lot of fighting.
sentences.zh: 当时发生了激烈的战斗。

sentences.en: And, you know, the fight went on from May of 1948 until early in 1949.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这场战斗从1948年5月一直持续到1949年初。

sentences.en: And the Israelis turned out to be stronger than the Arabs thought they would be.
sentences.zh: 以色列人表现出的实力比阿拉伯人预想的要强大。

sentences.en: And they were effective enough to defeat the Arab armies and roll them back and actually expand the boundaries of what became Israel beyond what the partition plan had provided.
sentences.zh: 他们不仅成功击退了阿拉伯军队，还反攻并扩大了以色列的疆域，超出了当初分治计划所划定的范围。

sentences.en: Now, what they didn't get at that time was the Gaza Strip, which was in the hands of Egypt.
sentences.zh: 当时他们没能拿下加沙地带，那里处于埃及的控制之下。

sentences.en: That remained in Egyptian hands.
sentences.zh: 那片地区仍由埃及掌控。

sentences.en: And they didn't get the West Bank of the Jordan River, which was in the hands of Jordan and remained so until the 1967 war.
sentences.zh: 他们也没能拿下约旦河西岸，那里由约旦控制，直到1967年战争前一直如此。

sentences.en: And they also didn't get all of Jerusalem.
sentences.zh: 他们也没能完全占领耶路撒冷。

sentences.en: And David, now that we're not just speaking about narratives, but about established historical facts, what happens to the Arabs on the lands that are in question
sentences.zh: 大卫，既然我们现在谈论的不仅仅是叙事，而是既定的历史事实，那么在这一时期，当以色列在对阵这些阿拉伯国家取得胜利时，身处争议土地上的阿拉伯人遭遇了什么？

sentences.en: during this period when Israel is achieving these victories against these Arab countries?
sentences.zh: 在这一时期，当以色列在对阵这些阿拉伯国家取得胜利时，身处争议土地上的阿拉伯人遭遇了什么？

sentences.en: So, it's true that an estimated 700,000 Arabs left what is now Israel.
sentences.zh: 确实，据估计有70万阿拉伯人离开了现在的以色列。

sentences.en: And they did so for a variety of reasons.
sentences.zh: 他们离开的原因多种多样。

sentences.en: Some fled the way people do in war, which is just to avoid the fighting.
sentences.zh: 有些人像战争中的普通民众一样逃离，仅仅是为了躲避战火。

sentences.en: And some fled because Arab leaders told them to get out pending a victory by the Arab forces after which they could come back.
sentences.zh: 有些人逃离是因为阿拉伯领导人告诉他们先撤离，等阿拉伯军队获胜后再回来。

sentences.en: Some were expelled deliberately, as we now know, by Israeli forces.
sentences.zh: 正如我们现在所知，有些人是被以色列军队蓄意驱逐的。

sentences.en: Some fled because they were afraid that they would be massacred.
sentences.zh: 有些人逃离是因为害怕遭到屠杀。

sentences.en: And there were massacres of civilians by Israeli forces.
sentences.zh: 当时确实发生了以色列军队屠杀平民的事件。

sentences.en: The most infamous was Diri Yassin, a village right on the outskirts of Jerusalem.
sentences.zh: 最臭名昭著的就是代尔亚辛村事件，那是一个位于耶路撒冷郊外的村庄。

sentences.en: And that was known before the declassification of Israeli documents.
sentences.zh: 在以色列文件解密之前，这件事就已经广为人知了。

sentences.en: But once those documents became available,
sentences.zh: 但当这些文件公开后，

sentences.en: Benny Morris found about two dozen places where civilians were massacred.
sentences.zh: 本尼·莫里斯发现了大约二十几处平民被屠杀的地点。

sentences.en: And that scared a lot of other Arabs who'd heard about them.
sentences.zh: 这吓坏了许多听说过这些事件的阿拉伯人。

sentences.en: And even where there was no violence or demands that they leave, people fled because they were afraid that the Israeli forces coming in would massacre them.
sentences.zh: 即使在没有暴力或驱逐要求的地方，人们也因为害怕进入的以色列军队会屠杀他们而逃离。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, those are the reasons, the basic reasons.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些就是基本原因。

sentences.en: And what the Palestinian narrative has done is to
sentences.zh: 而巴勒斯坦的叙事所做的，就是

sentences.en: put all of the departures in the category of deliberate expulsions.
sentences.zh: 将所有的离散都归类为蓄意驱逐。

sentences.en: And that is an exaggeration.
sentences.zh: 这是一种夸大。

sentences.en: But all the other reasons that people left don't really lessen the pain that has been passed down generation to generation
sentences.zh: 但人们离开的其他所有原因，并不能减轻巴勒斯坦人代代相传的痛苦，

sentences.en: by the Palestinians, which still animates their cause and fuels their desire to return.
sentences.zh: 这种痛苦至今仍激励着他们的事业，并助长了他们回归的渴望。

sentences.en: So, not only did Israelis expel Palestinians, despite the narrative that they didn't, some Israelis participated in the killing of Arab civilians during this conflict.
sentences.zh: 所以，不仅是以色列人驱逐了巴勒斯坦人（尽管叙事中否认这一点），一些以色列人在这场冲突中也参与了杀害阿拉伯平民的行动。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And when all this information is disclosed from these declassified documents in the archives, it reveals that the Israeli myth is just that.
sentences.zh: 当所有这些信息从档案中的解密文件披露出来时，它揭示了以色列的神话仅仅是神话而已。

sentences.en: It's a myth.
sentences.zh: 那是一个神话。

sentences.en: It's very sanitized.
sentences.zh: 它被美化得非常彻底。

sentences.en: By the way, the Palestinian myth is also a myth.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，巴勒斯坦人的神话也是神话。

sentences.en: So, you have this clash of narratives, which you can also call clash of myths.
sentences.zh: 所以，你面对的是这种叙事的冲突，也可以称之为神话的冲突。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, to that point, when we think about that Palestinian narrative, that claim inherited through many generations that the 700,000 Palestinians who left Israel were expelled from
sentences.zh: 说到这一点，当我们思考那种巴勒斯坦叙事时，即那种代代相传的说法，称那70万离开以色列的巴勒斯坦人在以色列建国期间被驱逐出

sentences.en: their homes during the creation of Israel, the story you're saying is more nuanced.
sentences.zh: 家园，你所说的故事其实更为微妙。

sentences.en: It's more complicated than that.
sentences.zh: 情况比那要复杂得多。

sentences.en: In part, because Israel was attacked and attacked back.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是由于以色列遭到了攻击，并进行了反击。

sentences.en: And there's an open war.
sentences.zh: 当时爆发了公开的战争。

sentences.en: Like you said, some Palestinians are leaving for fear of that war.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，一些巴勒斯坦人是因为害怕战争而离开的。

sentences.en: Some are leaving because they are being expelled.
sentences.zh: 一些人是因为被驱逐而离开的。

sentences.en: Some are leaving because they fear that they could be expelled or, worse, massacred.
sentences.zh: 一些人是因为害怕被驱逐，或者更糟，害怕被屠杀而离开的。

sentences.en: And there's no doubt that all forms of that kind of dislocation have to be wrenchingly painful.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，所有形式的这种流离失所必然是极其痛苦的。

sentences.en: But in a conflict where the details matter and are constantly being litigated, the historical
sentences.zh: 但在一个细节至关重要且不断被争论的冲突中，根据你的说法，历史

sentences.en: record, from what you're saying, makes clear that not all 700,000 Palestinians were expelled forcibly by Israel as a matter of policy.
sentences.zh: 记录清楚地表明，并非所有70万巴勒斯坦人都是作为以色列政策的一部分被强行驱逐的。

sentences.en: It might be more accurate to say that many of these Palestinians had to leave their homes as a result of a war.
sentences.zh: 更准确的说法可能是，许多巴勒斯坦人是因为战争而不得不离开家园。

sentences.en: I think that puts it very well, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这样表述非常准确，是的。

sentences.en: I mean, there are lots of reasons that people left.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人们离开的原因有很多。

sentences.en: The war at the core of it, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，核心还是战争。

sentences.en: And it's pretty ugly war is, you know, terrible things happen.
sentences.zh: 战争非常残酷，你知道，可怕的事情总会发生。

sentences.en: And they did in 1948.
sentences.zh: 1948年确实发生了。

sentences.en: Now, in some places, they were allowed to come back.
sentences.zh: 在某些地方，他们被允许回来。

sentences.en: But most of the Arabs who left or were driven out during the 48 war were never allowed to return to their homes inside what is now Israel.
sentences.zh: 但大多数在48年战争期间离开或被驱逐的阿拉伯人，从未被允许回到现在以色列境内的家中。

sentences.en: It's probably worth noting also that many Arabs did not leave and stayed in Israel.
sentences.zh: 值得注意的是，许多阿拉伯人并没有离开，而是留在了以色列。

sentences.en: And now they and their descendants make up about 20% of Israel's population.
sentences.zh: 现在他们及其后代占以色列人口的20%左右。

sentences.en: So, David, at the end of the 1948 war, when Israel emerges victorious, what does the world look like for both of these peoples?
sentences.zh: 那么，大卫，在1948年战争结束时，当以色列取得胜利，这两个民族的世界变成了什么样？

sentences.en: Israelis as well as Palestinians who have, through a combination of expulsions and flight, are not on their lands?
sentences.zh: 无论是以色列人，还是那些因驱逐和逃亡而流离失所的巴勒斯坦人？

sentences.en: Well, at that point, Israel was trying to build up their resilience and build up their economy and fulfill their dream of building a Jewish state.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那时以色列正试图增强韧性，发展经济，并实现建立犹太国家的梦想。

sentences.en: And it wasn't just Palestinians who were displaced.
sentences.zh: 流离失所的不仅仅是巴勒斯坦人。

sentences.en: Many Jews living in Arab countries were expelled by those countries and fled of their own accord sometimes.
sentences.zh: 许多居住在阿拉伯国家的犹太人也被这些国家驱逐，有时也是自愿逃离的。

sentences.en: Israel today, where at least half of the population are now descended from Jews who lived in Arab countries.
sentences.zh: 今天的以色列，至少有一半人口是那些曾居住在阿拉伯国家的犹太人的后裔。

sentences.en: And the Palestinians?
sentences.zh: 那巴勒斯坦人呢？

sentences.en: Well, the Palestinians were scattered into a diaspora in many countries around the world.
sentences.zh: 嗯，巴勒斯坦人散居在世界各地的许多国家。

sentences.en: But the bulk of them, at least at first, ended up in refugee camps in Lebanon, Syria, Jordan,
sentences.zh: 但他们中的大多数，起初都落脚在黎巴嫩、叙利亚、约旦的难民营中，

sentences.en: which controlled the West Bank at the time, and in the Gaza Strip, which was under Egyptian control.
sentences.zh: 当时约旦控制着西岸，而加沙地带则处于埃及的控制之下。

sentences.en: So that diaspora, so to speak, which ended up in the refugee camps, is still conscious of its origins and has passed down through the generations the story of displacement.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些最终进入难民营的流散群体，依然有着强烈的起源意识，并将流离失所的故事代代相传。

sentences.en: David, why wasn't there a creation of a Palestinian state after Israel's victory?
sentences.zh: 大卫，为什么以色列获胜后没有建立一个巴勒斯坦国？

sentences.en: Because there are still these people who had been promised through the partition a country, just as the people of Israel had been promised a country.
sentences.zh: 因为还有这些人，他们曾通过分治计划被承诺拥有一个国家，就像以色列人民被承诺拥有一个国家一样。

sentences.en: Why didn't a Palestinian state emerge in the aftermath of this war?
sentences.zh: 为什么战争结束后没有出现一个巴勒斯坦国？

sentences.en: Remember that this was a war not between the Palestinians and the Israelis.
sentences.zh: 记住，这并不是巴勒斯坦人和以色列人之间的战争。

sentences.en: This was a war between Arab countries and the new state of Israel.
sentences.zh: 这是阿拉伯国家与新生的以色列国之间的战争。

sentences.en: So at the end of the War of 1948, armistice agreements were signed that established the borders of Israel.
sentences.zh: 所以1948年战争结束时，签署的停战协议确立了以色列的边界。

sentences.en: And what wasn't Israel was Arab states.
sentences.zh: 而以色列之外的地方就是阿拉伯国家。

sentences.en: So there was no talk that I'm aware of, of creating a so-called Palestinian state.
sentences.zh: 所以我没听说过当时有关于建立所谓巴勒斯坦国的讨论。

sentences.en: I don't know that the concept was in the conversation at that point.
sentences.zh: 我不认为当时对话中存在这个概念。

sentences.en: Through the years, despite lip service given to the Palestinian cause by Arab leaders,
sentences.zh: 多年来，尽管阿拉伯领导人对巴勒斯坦事业口头上表示支持，

sentences.en: their interest in supporting that cause has been, aside from being rhetorical, has really been wanting.
sentences.zh: 但除了修辞上的支持外，他们对该事业的实际兴趣确实很匮乏。

sentences.en: You know, the Palestinians were not accepted as citizens, by and large, in the Arab countries where they fled.
sentences.zh: 你知道，巴勒斯坦人在他们逃往的阿拉伯国家中，基本上没有被接纳为公民。

sentences.en: Palestinians have been victims of the Arab world as well as of the Israelis.
sentences.zh: 巴勒斯坦人既是阿拉伯世界的受害者，也是以色列人的受害者。

sentences.en: And what is life like for these Palestinians as refugees in the period after the war?
sentences.zh: 那么，这些巴勒斯坦难民在战后的生活是怎样的？

sentences.en: The population was very impoverished.
sentences.zh: 当时的人口非常贫困。

sentences.en: The refugee camps began as tent camps.
sentences.zh: 难民营最初是帐篷营地。

sentences.en: They're still called camps, although that's a misnomer.
sentences.zh: 它们现在仍被称为“营地”，尽管这个称呼并不准确。

sentences.en: They've become established sluMs.
sentences.zh: 它们已经变成了固定的贫民窟。

sentences.en: The poverty rate is still fairly high.
sentences.zh: 贫困率仍然相当高。

sentences.en: It's very difficult for Palestinians to have a comfortable and prosperous life when they're confined to the camps.
sentences.zh: 当巴勒斯坦人被限制在营地里时，想要过上舒适富裕的生活是非常困难的。

sentences.en: And lots of Palestinians have left the camps and have been able to emigrate to various countries in Europe, in the United States.
sentences.zh: 许多巴勒斯坦人离开了营地，能够移民到欧洲和美国的各个国家。

sentences.en: And so those folks are doing better.
sentences.zh: 那些人过得好一些。

sentences.en: But, you know, it's not so easy to get the visas.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，拿到签证并不容易。

sentences.en: It's not so easy to accumulate the money to make that change.
sentences.zh: 攒够钱去做出那种改变也不容易。

sentences.en: And there's an ideological resistance to doing it, too.
sentences.zh: 而且在思想上也有抵触情绪。

sentences.en: I remember at one point when I was there, Israel wanted to build housing outside refugee camps in Gaza.
sentences.zh: 我记得有一次我在那里时，以色列想在加沙的难民营外建造住房。

sentences.en: And the local Palestinians rejected the idea vehemently because they thought it was an effort to undermine their status as refugees,
sentences.zh: 当地的巴勒斯坦人强烈拒绝了这个想法，因为他们认为这是在试图削弱他们作为难民的地位，

sentences.en: to basically do what's now called normalize the occupation.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是为了实现现在所说的“占领常态化”。

sentences.en: So there's a whole history of attempting to keep alive the idea of displacement, the refugee status, and the yearning to return.
sentences.zh: 所以，这里有一整段试图维持流离失所观念、难民身份和回归渴望的历史。

sentences.en: And from the Israeli point of view, the idea of return for these Palestinians represents what?
sentences.zh: 那么从以色列的角度来看，这些巴勒斯坦人的“回归”意味着什么？

sentences.en: A threat to the existence of the Jewish state for two reasons.
sentences.zh: 意味着对犹太国家生存的威胁，原因有二。

sentences.en: One, the Jews would be outnumbered by the Arabs in the voting rolls.
sentences.zh: 第一，在投票权上，犹太人的人数会被阿拉伯人超过。

sentences.en: Right now, if you take the West Bank and Gaza and Israel proper altogether in East Jerusalem,
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你把西岸、加沙、以色列本土以及东耶路撒冷加在一起，

sentences.en: the population division is about even, maybe even slightly tipped toward the Arab side.
sentences.zh: 人口比例大致相当，甚至可能稍微向阿拉伯一方倾斜。

sentences.en: So in an open, pluralistic, fair, free democracy, Arabs would outvote Jews.
sentences.zh: 因此，在一个开放、多元、公平、自由的民主国家，阿拉伯人的选票会超过犹太人。

sentences.en: So that's one issue.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个问题。

sentences.en: The other is the security concerns.
sentences.zh: 另一个是安全担忧。

sentences.en: I mean, we've just seen it in the Hamas attacks where Israeli Jews were attacked in their homes, in their kibbutzim.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们刚刚在哈马斯的袭击中看到了，以色列犹太人在家中、在基布兹里遭到袭击。

sentences.en: And the notion that, you know, lots of Palestinians would be allowed to come in and live inside Israel terrifies Israelis.
sentences.zh: 那种认为大量巴勒斯坦人会被允许进入并居住在以色列境内的想法，让以色列人感到恐惧。

sentences.en: David, we've spent a lot of time here trying to understand narratives and reality.
sentences.zh: 大卫，我们花了很多时间试图理解叙事和现实。

sentences.en: But the more time you spend understanding 1948 and the context surrounding it,
sentences.zh: 但你花在理解1948年及其背景上的时间越多，

sentences.en: it seems the thing that becomes very clear is that Palestinians and Israelis emerged from it with a strong claim to being victiMs.
sentences.zh: 似乎有一点变得非常清晰：巴勒斯坦人和以色列人在那场战争后，都强烈地认为自己是受害者。

sentences.en: Israelis are victims of Arab countries seeking Israel's destruction at the moment of its birth.
sentences.zh: 以色列人是阿拉伯国家在以色列诞生之初寻求摧毁它的受害者。

sentences.en: And the forces of anti-Semitism that led to the Holocaust and in the minds of so many Israelis necessitated Israel in the first place.
sentences.zh: 也是导致大屠杀的反犹主义势力的受害者，在许多以色列人看来，这正是以色列建国的必要性所在。

sentences.en: Palestinians are victims of the war that results from Israel's creation,
sentences.zh: 巴勒斯坦人是以色列建国所引发战争的受害者，

sentences.en: including Israeli tactics that forced many of them from their homes and later by the rejection that Palestinians faced from their Arab neighbors.
sentences.zh: 包括以色列迫使他们许多人离开家园的战术，以及后来巴勒斯坦人遭到阿拉伯邻国排斥的经历。

sentences.en: And the fact that Israel won the war and Palestinians and their allies lost doesn't really change their view of themselves as victiMs.
sentences.zh: 而以色列赢得了战争、巴勒斯坦人及其盟友输掉了战争这一事实，并没有改变他们视自己为受害者的看法。

sentences.en: Exactly right, Michael.
sentences.zh: 完全正确，迈克尔。

sentences.en: Exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: They are both victiMs.
sentences.zh: 他们都是受害者。

sentences.en: I remember an Israeli telling me once, when you put two victims together, it's like mixing fire and kerosene.
sentences.zh: 我记得一位以色列人曾对我说，当你把两个受害者放在一起时，就像把火和煤油混在一起。

sentences.en: Neither side recognizes the other's victimhood.
sentences.zh: 双方都不承认对方的受害者身份。

sentences.en: Although you have to say that there are some Israelis who do see the Palestinians as victims, even of the 48 war.
sentences.zh: 尽管你不得不说，确实有一些以色列人将巴勒斯坦人视为受害者，即使是在48年战争中也是如此。

sentences.en: After the declassification of documents showing that there were expulsions of Arabs,
sentences.zh: 在解密文件显示存在驱逐阿拉伯人的事实后，

sentences.en: that fact worked its way into some Israeli textbooks at the university level.
sentences.zh: 这一事实被写进了一些大学水平的以色列教科书中。

sentences.en: And then also at the secondary school level, to an extent, I think Israelis have come to see that there were such expulsions and there were injustices.
sentences.zh: 在中学阶段，在一定程度上，我认为以色列人也开始意识到确实存在过这种驱逐和不公正。

sentences.en: But that has not overcome the sense of great pride and accomplishment in creating the state through that war of independence.
sentences.zh: 但这并没有克服他们通过那场独立战争建立国家所带来的巨大自豪感和成就感。

sentences.en: And there are some Palestinians who see Jewish victimhood, but when they speak publicly about it, they get themselves into trouble.
sentences.zh: 也有一些巴勒斯坦人看到了犹太人的受害者身份，但当他们公开谈论这一点时，他们会给自己惹上麻烦。

sentences.en: There was a professor at Al-Qud University in Jerusalem who used to teach a course on the Holocaust to Palestinian college students.
sentences.zh: 耶路撒冷的圣城大学曾有一位教授，他为巴勒斯坦大学生开设了一门关于大屠杀的课程。

sentences.en: And he actually took them to visit Auschwitz.
sentences.zh: 他甚至带他们去参观了奥斯威辛集中营。

sentences.en: And he got them to see Jews as victims and understand the historical roots of their arrival in this place, this Holy Land.
sentences.zh: 他让他们看到了犹太人作为受害者的一面，并理解了他们来到这片土地——这片圣地——的历史根源。

sentences.en: And what happened to him?
sentences.zh: 那他后来怎么样了？

sentences.en: He was threatened and ultimately he was fired.
sentences.zh: 他受到了威胁，最终被解雇了。

sentences.en: So the obstacles to seeing the other and recognizing what the other has gone through are immense.
sentences.zh: 所以，想要看到对方并承认对方所经历的一切，障碍是巨大的。

sentences.en: They're immense.
sentences.zh: 障碍是巨大的。

sentences.en: So we have here a conflict between two peoples who are victims of each other, but not only of each other, also of the larger world.
sentences.zh: 所以我们面对的是两个民族之间的冲突，他们互为受害者，但不仅是互为受害者，也是更大世界的受害者。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And in this case, how you understand the conflict and how you understand the whole question of victimhood depends very much on where you start the clock,
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，你如何理解这场冲突，如何理解受害者身份的整个问题，很大程度上取决于你从哪里开始计时，

sentences.en: where you think the story begins.
sentences.zh: 取决于你认为故事是从哪里开始的。

sentences.en: Exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: David, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 大卫，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们真的很感激。

sentences.en: Thanks for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听。

sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 已倒闭的加密货币交易所 FTX 的创始人萨姆·班克曼-弗里德（Sam Bankman-Fried），

sentences.en: was convicted on all charges of fraud and conspiracy on Thursday after a month-long trial that exposed the hubris and risk-taking across the crypto industry.
sentences.zh: 周四在经过一个月的审判后，被判犯有所有欺诈和共谋罪名。这场审判揭露了整个加密货币行业中存在的傲慢与冒险行为。

sentences.en: The conviction puts Bankman-Fried in league with the biggest financial fraudsters in history.
sentences.zh: 此次定罪使班克曼-弗里德跻身于历史上最严重的金融诈骗犯之列。

sentences.en: Overall, his victims lost nearly $10 billion in funds.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，他的受害者损失了近 100 亿美元的资金。

sentences.en: And he now faces a sentence of up to 110 years in prison.
sentences.zh: 他现在面临最高 110 年的监禁。

sentences.en: And on Thursday,
sentences.zh: 而在周四，

sentences.en: the Israeli military said it had encircled Gaza City and was waging close-quarters combat with Hamas as they push forward with what Israeli officials have predicted will be a long and bloody ground invasion.
sentences.zh: 以色列军方表示，他们已经包围了加沙城，并正在与哈马斯进行近距离交战，同时推进以色列官员所预言的长期且血腥的地面入侵。

sentences.zh: 早上好，这里是拉法。

sentences.zh: 我刚到达过境点。

sentences.en: They're going to start calling people.
sentences.zh: 他们马上要开始叫名字了。

sentences.en: I know my name is on the list, but I don't know when I will enter.
sentences.zh: 我知道名单上有我的名字，但我不知道什么时候能进去。

sentences.en: The evacuation of foreign nationals and wounded Palestinians from Gaza into Egypt entered its second day on Thursday.
sentences.zh: 周四，外国公民和受伤的巴勒斯坦人从加沙撤离至埃及的行动进入了第二天。

sentences.en: Among those leaving was Wafa El Saka, the subject of a daily episode on October 16th.
sentences.zh: 离开的人群中包括 Wafa El Saka，她是 10 月 16 日那一期节目的主角。

sentences.en: When the war broke out, El Saka, an American citizen who had grown up in Gaza, became trapped in Gaza, where she was visiting family.
sentences.zh: 战争爆发时，在加沙长大的美国公民 El Saka 正好在加沙探亲，因此被困在那里。

sentences.en: I'm glad that I'm going to go and meet with my grandson and my husband and my boys and their wives.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴我能去见我的孙子、丈夫、儿子以及他们的妻子们了。

sentences.en: At 1.30 p.m.
sentences.zh: 下午 1 点 30 分，

sentences.en: local time on Thursday, she crossed into Egypt, then boarded a minivan with other Americans, bound for Cairo.
sentences.zh: 周四当地时间，她进入了埃及，随后与其他美国人一起登上了一辆前往开罗的小型货车。

sentences.en: I don't know how I feel.
sentences.zh: 我不知道自己是什么感觉。

sentences.en: I left my whole family behind.
sentences.zh: 我把我的整个家庭都留在了身后。

sentences.en: Needed my help, but I couldn't help them.
sentences.zh: 他们需要我的帮助，但我却帮不了他们。

sentences.en: But I need to go to my other family, too.
sentences.zh: 但我必须去见我的另一个家庭。

sentences.en: I don't know why we have to choose.
sentences.zh: 我不知道为什么我们必须做出选择。

sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。
